# b) (@owner@'s) <whatever> of/on @<primary school>@ and @<secondary school>@
# c) (@owner@'s) <whatever> of/on @<secondary school adj>@ @<primary school>@

# These are used in messages like "@The_monster@ calls down the wrath of @possessive_God@ upon @target@.",
# where @possessive_God@ is replaced with "its god", etc.
# "His" is only used for male uniques, which will be masculine in German.
# "Her" is used for female uniques plus harpies and nymphs, which are all feminine in German.
# "Its" is used for most non-unique monsters, but they can be masculine, feminine or neuter in German.
# "Their" is used for gender-neutral uniques - this doesn't work in German.
# Therefore, we use "a god" instead of "its/their god".

###############################################################################
#
# German grammar
#
# Entries named GENERATE:<context> are used to transform a string from the
# default (null) context into the version for <context>. These are only applied
# if there is no hardcoded definition of the string for <context>.
#
# The bodies of the entries consist of a sequence of regular expressions (regex).
# If you are not familiar with regular expressions, consult Google.
#
# Expressions come in two forms:
# /pattern/replacement/
# /substring-pattern/pattern/replacement/
#
# The first type replaces all instances of pattern in the string with replacement.
# The second type only does the replacement within the first substring matching
# substring-pattern.
#
# Expressions are applied in order. Each expression is applied to the result of
# the previous expression (not the original string).
#
# German-specific notes:
#  - We want to decline only up to the first noun. If there are subsequent nouns,
#    they will be in their own case, and should be left alone. For example:
#    "der {adj-e}@adj@Ring der Schatten" - don't change the part after Ring
#    "ein {adj-er}@adj@Ring magischer Kraft" - ditto
#    "ein {adj-es}@adj@Paar {adj-e}@adj@Handschuhe" - don't change the part after Paar
#  - The default form (null context) for nouns is nominative
#  - The default form (null context) for adjectives is the -e form
#
###############################################################################

#################################
# Pregeneration
#################################

# Note: These are run in numbered order, and the results of earlier runs are
# available to later runs (and later runs must take into account the fact that
# the results of the earlier runs exist).

#############
# select all nouns with definite article and generate a version with an
# adjective placeholder after the article
%%%%
PREGENERATE:0

SELECT_BY_KEY:/^the [^@]/

# English
KEY:/^the /the @adj@/
# "pair of boots/gloves" needs a second adjective placeholder
KEY:/pair of (.*)/pair of @adj2@$1/

# German
# nominative singular
/^((\{m\})?der|(\{f\})?die|(\{n\})?das) /$1 {adj-e}@adj@/
# plural and genitive
/^(\{pl\}die|\{f\}der|\{n\}des|\{m\}des|des) /$1 {adj-en}@adj@/
# "pair of boots/gloves" (but not quick blades) needs a second adjective placeholder
/Paar (.*)/Paar {adj-e}@adj2@$1/
%%%%

#############
# generate indefinite nominative from definite nominative
%%%%
PREGENERATE:1

SELECT_BY_KEY:/^the .*[^']{2}$/

# transform (English) key
KEY:/^the (one-)/a $1/
KEY:/^the ([aeiouAEIOU])/an $1/
KEY:/^the /a /

# articles
/^(\{m\})?der /{m}ein /
/^(\{f\})?die /{f}eine /
/^(\{n\})?das /{n}ein /
# plural
/^\{pl\}die /{pl}/

# masc adjectives
/^\{m\}ein [^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/e\b/er/

# fix some special cases
/e (Drakonier|Yiuf)/er $1/

# neuter adjectives
/^\{n\}ein [^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/e\b/es/

# plural adjectives
/^\{pl\}[^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/en\b/e/
%%%%

#############
# generate indefinite possessive from definite posessive
%%%%
PREGENERATE:2

SELECT_BY_KEY:/^the .*('s|')$/

# transform (English) key
KEY:/^the (one-)/a $1/
KEY:/^the ([aeiouAEIOU])/an $1/
KEY:/^the /a /

# articles
/^(\{f\})?der /einer /
/^des /eines /
%%%%

#############
# generate "your" (nominative and possessive) from indefinite
# (easier than generating from definite because adjectives will already be in the right form)
%%%%
PREGENERATE:3

SELECT_BY_KEY:/^(a|an) /

# transform (English) key
KEY:/^(a|an) /your /

# singular
/^(\{[mfn]\})?ein/$1dein/

# plural
/^\{pl\}[^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/e\b/en/
/^\{pl\}/{pl}deine /
%%%%

#############
# player ghost/illusion can have no determiner in English, but needs definite article in German
%%%%
PREGENERATE:4

SELECT_BY_KEY:/^the (@adj@)?@name@'s/

KEY:/^the //
%%%%

#############
# generate no determiner (nominative) from indefinite
%%%%
PREGENERATE:5

# exclude possessives
SELECT_BY_KEY:/^(a|an) .*[^']{2}$/

# remove article from key
KEY:/^(a|an) //

# remove article from value
/^(\{m\})?ein /{m}/
/^(\{f\})?eine /{f}/
/^\{n\}ein /{n}/

# if there are now two context markers in a row, remove the first one (it's superfluous).
/^\{.\}\{/{/
%%%%

#############
# generate counted plural with adjective placeholder from counted plural without
PREGENERATE:6

SELECT_BY_KEY:/^@num@ [^@]/

KEY:/^@num1@ /@num2@ @adj@/

/^(\{pl\})?@num1@ /{pl}@num2@ {adj-e}@adj@/
%%%%

#############
# generate uncounted plural from counted plural without
PREGENERATE:7

SELECT_BY_KEY:/^@num@ /

KEY:/^@num@ //

/^(\{pl\})?@num@ /{pl}/
%%%%

#############
# generate definite plural from counted plural
PREGENERATE:8

SELECT_BY_KEY:/^@num@ /

KEY:/^@num@/the/

/^(\{pl\})?@num@/{pl}die/
%%%%

#############
# English possessive translates to German genitive (or von + dative for named monsters).
# Re-use these entries for the situation when English nominative has to be translated
# to German genitive.
%%%%
PREGENERATE:9

SELECT_BY_KEY:/'s$/

# only the English key needs to change
KEY:/^(.*)'s$/{gen}$1/
%%%%

#############
# if adjective already has a context, we can't generate other forms on the fly, so pre-generate
%%%%
PREGENERATE:10
SELECT_BY_KEY:/^\{adj-e\}/
KEY:/^\{adj-e\}/{adj-er}/
/e$/er/
%%%%
PREGENERATE:11
SELECT_BY_KEY:/^\{adj-e\}/
KEY:/^\{adj-e\}/{adj-es}/
/e$/es/
%%%%
PREGENERATE:12
SELECT_BY_KEY:/^\{adj-e\}/
KEY:/^\{adj-e\}/{adj-en}/
/e$/en/
%%%%
PREGENERATE:13
SELECT_BY_KEY:/^\{adj-e\}/
KEY:/^\{adj-e\}/{adj-em}/
/e$/em/
%%%%

#################################
# Adjectives
#################################
%%%%
GENERATE:adj-er
/e\b/er/
%%%%
GENERATE:adj-es
/e\b/es/
%%%%
GENERATE:adj-en
/e\b/en/
%%%%
GENERATE:adj-em
/e\b/em/
%%%%

#################################
# Accusative case
#################################
%%%%
GENERATE:acc

# determiners
/^\{m\}der /{m}den /
/^\{m\}ein /{m}einen /
/^\{m\}dein /{m}deinen /

# masc adjectives
/^\{m\}den [^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/e /en /
/^\{m\}den [^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/\{adj-e\}/{adj-en}/
/^\{m\}[^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/er /en /
/^\{m\}[^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/\{adj-er\}/{adj-en}/

# weak nouns
/(Akolyth)\b/$1en/
/[A-ZÄÖÜ][^ ,]+/(Mensch|[Bb]är|[^e]ist|ant|taur|myzet|[Ff]ürst)$/$1en/
/[A-ZÄÖÜ][^ ,]+/([Ss]chamane|[Ss]chütze|Sklave|[Hh]err|loge|mycete)$/$1n/
/[A-ZÄÖÜ][^ ,]+/([Rr]iese|[Dd]rache|[Dd]ruide|[Hh]eilige|Ahne)$/$1n/
# match Affe but not Waffe
/[A-ZÄÖÜ][^ ,]+/(Affe|[^Ww]affe)$/$1n/

# fix special cases
/ der Ork/ den Ork/
/er? Yiuf/en Yiuf/
# make sure it's not plural
/^\{m\}.*/er Drakonier/en Drakonier/

%%%%

#################################
# Dative case
#################################
%%%%
GENERATE:dat

# remove masc/neut gender hint, to simplify following regexps
/^\{(m|n)\}//

# masc/neut determiners
/^(der|das) /dem /
/^ein /einem /
/^dein /deinem /

# masc/neut adjectives
/^(d|ein|dein)em [^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/e[rs]? /en /
/^(d|ein|dein)em [^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/\{adj-e[rs]?\}/{adj-en}/
/^[^A-ZÄÖÜ ][^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/e[rs] /em /
/^[^A-ZÄÖÜ ][^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/\{adj-e[rs]\}/{adj-em}/

# mark plurals, if not already marked
/^(die |deine )?(@num@|[0-9]+) /^(.)/{pl}$1/

# plural determiners
/^\{pl\}die /{pl}den /
/^\{pl\}deine /{pl}deinen /

# fem determiners
/^(\{f\})?die /der /
/^(\{f\})?eine /einer /
/^(\{f\})?deine /deiner /

# plural adjectives
/^\{pl\}[^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/e /en /
/^\{pl\}[^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/\{adj-e\}/{adj-en}/

# fem adjectives
/^(\{f\})?(der|einer|deiner) [^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/e /en /
/^(\{f\})?(der|einer|deiner) [^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/\{adj-e\}/{adj-en}/
/^[^A-ZÄÖÜ ][^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/e /er /
/^[^A-ZÄÖÜ ][^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/\{adj-e\}/{adj-er}/

# plural nouns
/^\{pl\}.*[A-ZÄÖÜ][^ ,]+/([^snai])$/$1n/

# weak nouns
/(Akolyth)\b/$1en/
/[A-ZÄÖÜ][^ ,]+/(Mensch|[Bb]är|[^e]ist|ant|taur|myzet|[Ff]ürst|herz)$/$1en/
/[A-ZÄÖÜ][^ ,]+/([Ss]chamane|[Ss]chütze|Sklave|[Hh]err|loge|mycete)$/$1n/
/[A-ZÄÖÜ][^ ,]+/([Rr]iese|[Dd]rache|[Dd]ruide|[Hh]eilige|Ahne)$/$1n/
# match Affe but not Waffe
/[A-ZÄÖÜ][^ ,]+/(Affe|[^Ww]affe)$/$1n/

# remove fem/plural gender hint
/^\{(f|pl)\}//

# fix special cases
/Blork der Ork/Blork dem Ork/
/er? (Yiuf|Drakonier)/em $1/
/^(dem|einem|deinem) (.*)em (Yiuf|Drakonier)/$1 $2en $3/
/^(der|einer|deiner) (.*)Lernäische Hydra/$1 $2Lernäischen Hydra/
/Lernäische Hydra/Lernäischer Hydra/
# nominalised adjective
/Unsichtbares\b/Unsichtbarem/

%%%%

#################################
# Genitive case
#################################
%%%%
GENERATE:gen

# mark genitive/dative suffix so we can exclude it from later expressions
/ (der|des|einer|eines|von|vom) /# $1 /

# remove gender hints, to simplify following regexps
/^\{(m|n|f|pl)\}//

# adjectives ending in -es
# (must do before adding -es to determiners)
/^[^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/es\b/en/

# masc/neut determiners
/^(der|das) /des /
/^ein /eines /
/^dein /deines /

# adjectives ending in -er
# (must do after removing -er from determiners)
/^[^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/er\b/en/

# masc/neut adjectives ending in -e
/^des [^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/e\b/en/

# fem/pl determiners
/^die /der /
/^eine /einer /
/^deine /deiner /

# fem/pl adjectives
/^(der|einer|deiner) [^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/e\b/en/
/^[^A-ZÄÖÜ]+/e\b/er/

# masc/neuter nouns
/^(?!(\{adj\-er\}|[a-zäöüß\-]+er ))[^#]*/([a-zäöü])$/$1s/

# remove mark we added
/#//

# Examples of high score entries (verbose format):
#
#  2. 1797852 Fred the Slayer (level 22, 226/229 HPs)
#             Began as a Minotaur Berserker on Jan 31, 2022.
#             Was an Elder of Trog.
#             Escaped with the Orb
#             ... and 3 runes!
#
#             The game lasted 02:00:23 (50312 turns).
#
# 16.  292913 Ziggy the Fighter (level 20, -5/159 HPs)
#             Began as a Demonspawn Fire Elementalist on Apr 7, 2023.
#             Was an Initiate of Gozag.
#             Killed from afar by a war gargoyle (42 damage)
#             ... with a spray of metal splinters
#             ... led by a peacekeeper
#             ... on level 4 of the Vaults on Apr 10, 2023.
#             The game lasted 06:34:14 (66612 turns).
#
# 40.      12 Bob the Digger (level 2, -3/20 HPs)
#             Began as a Meteoran Earth Elementalist on June 16, 2022.
#             Was a Follower of Nemelex Xobeh.
#             Slain by Terence
#             ... wielding a +0 flail
#              (7 damage)
#             ... on level 3 of the Dungeon.
#             The game lasted 00:02:01 (174 turns).

# @yyyy@ = full year

# unidentified potions can have 1 or 2 adjectives
# the adjective closest to the noun is a colour

# Some potion colours are the names of materials, and are used elsewhere
# in Crawl to mean actually made of/with that thing, rather than merely having
# its colour. In English, we can get away with using the same word for both
# meanings, but that's not necessarily the case in other languages.

# protection from fire and fire resistance are equivalent
# the former name is used on rings and the latter on armour
%%%%
" of protection from fire"
" der Feuerresistenz"
%%%%
" of fire resistance"
" der Feuerresistenz"
%%%%

# protection from cold and cold resistance are equivalent
# the former name is used on rings and the latter on armour
%%%%
" of protection from cold"
" der Kälteresistenz"
%%%%
" of cold resistance"
" der Kälteresistenz"
%%%%

# Attack strength punctuation
##############################
# Exclamation marks show amount of damage.
# The @arg@ is a placeholder for the sentence. It's done this way
# because some languages don't simply append punctuation to the end.
# For example, in Spanish, you would translate "@arg1@!" as "¡@arg2@!"

#
# Monster properties
#
# Used in a couple of places:
#  1. When targeting
#  2. When examining with xv in brackets after the monster name
#  3. On mouse hover, in the sentence: "This monster is @arg@."
#  4. In a message when monster comes into view
#
# For #3, a custom sentence is used for some props, instead of sticking the
# property string into the generic sentence above.
#
# Additionally, some properties have a different short form (some even have
# singular and plural short forms), but all the above places use the long form,
# so not sure where the short forms are used.
#

#
# Monsters - unique, definite article, nominative
#
###############################################################################

# Notes:
#
# It might seem weird to list named monsters with the definite article, but it's
# needed for messages like: "You hit the helpless Sigmund." Also, it's easier to
# generate the "plain" version (without article) from the one with the article
# than the other way round because it's very hard to identify plain unique names
# (there are hundreds of other one-word strings that start with a capital
# letter).
#
# Some uniques are gender-neutral in English. This is different to neuter.
# (neuter -> it, gender neutral -> they). While German has neuter, it can't do
# gender neutral, so in order to avoid calling people "it", we've used the
# genders those monsters had in older versions of Crawl.

%%%%

Du bist resistent gegen Schaden.

Du kannst dich selbst heilen, indem du magische Energie zuführst.

Du bist immun gegen Krankheit und Miasma.

Du kannst wilde Blitze spucken.

schädliche Dämpfe speien

Du kannst schädliche Dämpfe speien.

Du kannst Strahlen entzaubernder Energie speien.

Du kannst Feuer speien.

breathe frost
Frostodem

Du kannst Wellen eisiger Kälte speien, die Feinde zurückwerfen.

spit acid
Säure spucken

Du kannst Säureklumpen spucken.

permanent stasis
permanente Stasis
%%%%

Du kannst nicht geeilt, verlangsamt, in Berserkerwut versetzt, gelähmt oder teleportiert werden.

dig shafts and tunnels
Schächte und Tunnel graben

Du kannst durch Wände und zu einer tieferen Ebene graben.

almost no armour
fast keine Rüstung

Du kannst die meisten Arten von Rüstungen nicht tragen.

# Translations for player titles (without article)

# In German, more is required than just stripping the article:
#  - adjectives use the strong declension in the absence of an article
#  - ditto for nouns that are nominalised adjectives
#

###############################################################################
#
# Translations for status effects
#
# NOTE: short single-word strings starting with a capital letter are so-called
# "status lights", which appear in the status bar of the HUD. Since space there
# is limited, translations of these should also be kept short. Use abbreviations
# if necessary. Where these need to be disambiguated from other strings (e.g.
# spells of the same name, they are prefixed with {status}.
#
###############################################################################


##################
# status.cc
##################

#################################
# Recitations
#################################

# Each recitation is 3 lines, and these variables are always available:
#     @sinners@, @sin_adj@, @sin_noun@, @virtuous@, @virtue@, @smite@, @smitten@,
#     as well as these extras that are not used in the English version:
#     @the_sinners@, @the_sin_noun@, @the_virtue@, which are just @sinners@,
#     @sin_noun@ and @virtue@ prepended with the definite article ("the").
# The translation can use any of these variables freely at any time. It does not
# need to restrict itself to those variables used in the equivalent English line.
# (However, if you use a variable, you must provide translations for its values.)

%%%%
It was the word of Zin that there would not be @sin_noun@...
Es war das Wort von Zin, dass es {acc}@sin_noun@ nicht mehr geben würde...
%%%%
...and did the people not suffer until they had @smitten@...
...und hat das Volk nicht gelitten, bis es {acc}@the_sinners@...
%%%%
...the @sinners@, after which all was well?
...@smitten@ hatte, wonach alles gut war?
%%%%
The voice of Zin, pure and clear, did say that the @sinners@...
Die Stimme von Zin, rein und klar, sagte, dass @the_sinners@...
%%%%
...were not @virtuous@! And hearing this, the people rose up...
.. nicht @virtuous@ waren! Und als das Volk dies hörte, erhob es sich...
%%%%
...and embraced @virtue@, for they feared Zin's wrath.
...und nahm {acc}@the_virtue@ an, denn es fürchtete Zin's Zorn.
%%%%
Zin spoke of the doctrine of @virtue@, and...
Zin sprach von der Lehre {gen}@the_virtue@ und...
%%%%
...saw the @sinners@ filled with fear, for they were...
...sah {acc}@the_sinners@ von Furcht erfüllt, denn sie waren...
%%%%
...@sin_adj@ and knew Zin's wrath would come for them.
...@sin_adj@ und wussten, dass Zins Zorn sie finden würde.
%%%%
And so Zin bade the @sinners@ to come before...
Und so forderte Zin {acc}@the_sinners@ auf, vor den Altar...
%%%%
...the altar, that judgement might be passed...
...zu treten, damit das Urteil gefällt werden kann...
%%%%
...upon those who were not @virtuous@.
...über jene, die nicht @virtuous@ waren.
%%%%
To the devout, Zin provideth. From the rest...
Für die Frommen sorgt Zin. Vom Rest...
%%%%
...ye @sinners@, ye guilty...
...@sinners@, ihr, die...
%%%%
...of @sin_noun@, Zin taketh.
...{gen}@the_sin_noun@ schuldig seid, nimmt Zin.
%%%%
Zin saw the @sin_noun@ of the @sinners@, and...
Zin sah {acc}@the_sin_noun@ {gen}@the_sinners@ und...
%%%%
...was displeased, for did the law not say that...
...war verärgert. Denn sagt das Gesetz nicht, dass...
%%%%
...those who did not become @virtuous@ would be @smitten@?
...jene, die nicht @virtuous@ sind, @smitten@ werden?
%%%%
Zin said that @virtue@ shall be the law of the land, and...
Zin sagte, dass @virtue@ das geltende Recht sei und die, die sich...
%%%%
...those who turn to @sin_noun@ will be @smitten@. This was fair...
...{dat}@the_sin_noun@ zuwenden, @smitten@ werden sollen. Das war angemessen...
%%%%
...and just, and not a voice dissented.
...und gerecht und keine Stimme hat widersprochen.
%%%%
Damned, damned be the @sinners@ and...
Verdammt, verdammt seien @the_sinners@ und...
%%%%
...all else who abandon @virtue@! Let them...
...alle anderen, die {acc}@the_virtue@ aufgeben! Sie sollen...
%%%%
...be @smitten@ by the jurisprudence of Zin!
...von der Rechtsprechung Zins @smitten@ werden!
%%%%
And Zin said to all in attendance, 'Which of ye...
Und Zin sagte zu allen Anwesenden: 'Wer von euch...
%%%%
...number among the @sinners@? Come before me, that...
...zählt zu {dat}@the_sinners@? Kommt vor mich, dass...
%%%%
...I may @smite@ you now for your @sin_noun@!'
...ich euch für {acc}@the_sin_noun@ @smite@ kann!'
%%%%
Yea, I say unto thee, bring forth...
Wahrlich, ich sage euch, bringt {acc}@the_sinners@...
%%%%
...the @sinners@ that they may know...
...hervor, damit sie den Zorn Zins...
%%%%
...the wrath of Zin, and thus be @smitten@!
...erkennen dürfen und dafür @smitten@ werden!
%%%%
In a great set of silver scales are weighed the...
In einer großen silbernen Waage werden die Seelen...
%%%%
...souls of the @sinners@, and with their @sin_adj@...
...{gen}@the_sinners@ gewogen. Und weil sie {nom}@sin_adj@...
%%%%
...ways, the balance hath tipped against them!
...waren, hat sich das Gleichgewicht gegen sie gewandt!
%%%%
It is just that the @sinners@ shall be @smitten@...
Es ist gerecht, dass @the_sinners@ zur rechten Zeit @smitten@...
%%%%
...in due time, for @virtue@ is what Zin has declared...
...werden, denn @virtue@ ist das, was Zin als...
%%%%
...the law of the land, and Zin's word is law!
...geltendes Recht erklärt hat. Und das Wort von Zin ist Gesetz!
%%%%
Thus the people made the covenant of @virtue@ with...
So schloss das Volk den Bund {gen}@the_virtue@ mit...
%%%%
...Zin, and all was good, for they knew that the...
...Zin und alles war gut. Denn sie wussten, dass...
%%%%
...@sinners@ would trouble them no longer.
...@the_sinners@ sie nicht mehr stören würden.
%%%%
What of the @sinners@? @Smitten@ for their...
Und was ist mit {dat}@the_sinners@? @Smitten@ für...
%%%%
...@sin_noun@ they shall be! Zin will @smite@ them again...
...{acc}@the_sin_noun@ sollen sie sein! Zin wird sie wieder...
%%%%
...and again, and again!
...und wieder und wieder @smite@!
%%%%
And lo, the wrath of Zin did find...
Und sehet, der Zorn von Zin fand sie...
%%%%
...them wherever they hid, and the @sinners@...
...wo auch immer sie sich versteckten. Und @the_sinners@...
%%%%
...were @smitten@ for their @sin_noun@!
...wurden @smitten@ für {acc}@the_sin_noun@!
%%%%
Zin looked out upon the remains of the @sinners@...
Zin blickte auf die sterblichen Überreste {gen}@the_sinners@...
%%%%
...and declared it good that they had been...
...und erklärte es für gut, dass sie...
%%%%
...@smitten@. And thus justice was done.
...@smitten@ worden waren. Und so wurde der Gerechtigkeit Genüge getan.
%%%%
The law of Zin demands thee...
Das Gesetz von Zin verlangt von dir...
%%%%
...be @virtuous@, and that the punishment for @sin_noun@...
...@virtuous@ zu sein und dass die Strafe für {acc}@sin_noun@...
%%%%
...shall be swift and harsh!
...rasch und streng sein wird!
%%%%
It was then that Zin bade them...
Es war zu jener Zeit, dass Zin sie mahnte, nicht von...
%%%%
...not to stray from @virtue@, lest...
...{dat}@the_virtue@ abzuweichen, damit sie nicht...
%%%%
...they become as damned as the @sinners@.
...so verdammt würden wie @the_sinners@.
%%%%
Only the @virtuous@ shall be judged worthy, and...
Nur die, die @virtuous@ sind, werden für würdig befunden und...
%%%%
...all the @sinners@ will be found wanting. Such is...
...@the_sinners@ werden sich als unzulänglich erweisen...
%%%%
...the word of Zin, and such is the law!
...So lautet das Wort von Zin. Und so lautet das Gesetz!
%%%%
To those who would swear an oath of @virtue@ on my altar...
Denen, die auf meinem Altar den Eid {gen}@the_virtue@ schwören...
%%%%
...I bring ye salvation. To the rest, ye @sinners@...
...werde ich Erlösung bringen. Für den Rest, {acc}@the_sinners@...
%%%%
...and the @sin_adj@, the name of Zin shall be thy damnation.
...und jene, die @sin_adj@ sind, soll der Name Zins Verdammnis sein.
%%%%
And Zin decreed that the people would be...
Und Zin ordnete an, dass das Volk vor jeder Art...
%%%%
...protected from @sin_noun@ in all its forms, and...
...{gen}@the_sin_noun@ geschützt würde und...
%%%%
...preserved in their @virtue@ for all the days to come.
...in @virtue@ bewahrt sei für alle Tage.
%%%%
For those who would enter Zin's holy bosom...
Für jene, die in Zins heiligen Schoß gelangen wollen...
%%%%
...and live in @virtue@, Zin provideth. Such is...
...und in {dat}@virtue@ leben, ist durch Zin gesorgt. Dies ist...
%%%%
...the covenant, and such is the way of things.
...der Bund und dies ist der Lauf der Dinge.
%%%%
Zin hath not damned the @sinners@, but it is they...
Zin hat {acc}@the_sinners@ nicht verdammt, sondern sie sind es...
%%%%
...that have damned themselves for their @sin_noun@, for...
...die sich selbst verdammt haben mit {dat}@the_sin_noun@, denn...
%%%%
...did Zin not decree that to be @sin_adj@ was wrong?
